judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

central_claim.note: Conservative half of C1 (conservatives in liberal climates less hesitant); liberals-regardless half and booster uptake not stated.

evidence.note: Online survey, US, March to April 2023 (E1) without the nonprobability convenience sample or Qualtrics Panels; final N = 683 (E2) without the 1,777 collected and 970 screened out.

key_findings.note: Hesitancy half of F1 (positive main associations with vaccine and booster hesitancy, p.7); the vaccination and boosting half is not stated here.
Interaction significant for vaccine hesitancy, booster hesitancy and booster status (p.10), without the shape of any of them.
Liberal half of the hesitancy interaction (abstract).
Conservative half of F3 (60% vs under 35%); liberals boosted anywhere not stated.

scope_and_limits.note: Factors other than the vote-share proxy, e.g. population density, could drive the results.

theoretical_positioning.note: Prior research identified the separate impacts of orientation and climate; the paper examines their interaction.

interlocutor_claim.note: Conservatism associated with greater hesitancy (p.2, refs 6-12); quote also gives lower uptake.
